verdict.rationale: The SDK documents programmatic sandbox creation and command execution for agent workflows. Blocking commands and log streaming let an agent read results, and authentication is automatic in production, so provisioning, execution and result-reading run without a human. Teardown is the weak link: the evidence shows stopping from the Dashboard and a default 5-minute timeout, but no explicit SDK or CLI stop/delete call, so the end-to-end loop is not fully documented. missing for 10: explicit programmatic stop/delete API in the evidence, an explicit way to retrieve command stdout and exit code beyond log streaming, independent or hands-on corroboration of a fully autonomous agent loop.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, my agent can provision its own sandbox, execute code, read the results, and tear it down — end to end without a human

citations.quote: They provide a programmatic interface to create sandboxes, run commands, and manage files.
Run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs. Use Vercel Sandbox for agent workflows
Commands can run in blocking mode (wait for completion) or detached mode (return immediately).
Stream logs from a detached command
In production on Vercel, authentication is automatic.
The default timeout is 5 minutes. You can configure this using the `timeout` option when creating a sandbox
You can also stop sandboxes from the Vercel Dashboard by navigating to Observability > Sandboxes and clicking Stop Sandbox.
